test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 12 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A solid metallic sphere of radius 3 cm is melted and drawn into a wire of thickness 4 mm. What is the length of the wire (in m)?
solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the sphere = 3 cm

Thickness of the wire = 4 mm 

**Concept used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr3

Volume of a cylinder = πr2h

r = radius of the base of cylinder and radius of the sphere

h = length of height of the cylinder

**Calculation:**

Thickness 4 mm i.e diameter

So, radius = 2 mm

Now,

3 cm = 30 mm

According to the question,

Volume of the sphere = Volume of the wire

(4/3)π × 30³ = π2²h

⇒ 4 × 10 × 900 = 4h

⇒ 9000 = h

So, length of the wire = 9000 mm

But here we have asked the length of the wire in m

So, length = 9000/1000 = 9 m [∵ 1 m = 1000 mm]

**∴ The length of the wire (in m) is 9.**
